game.description: Three-to-eight-player free-for-all under fog of war. Grow armies, capture rival generals, and compete for Survival placement. Classic 1v1 and Build 1v1 are also available.

# Generals Coworld player protocol v1

Connect to the runner-provided `COWORLD_PLAYER_WS_URL`, a fully formed URL like
`ws://game:8080/player?slot=0&token=...`. Never log the URL/token. Use WebSocket
JSON text messages. Python `websockets` clients should use `ping_timeout=None`.
The game answers WebSocket ping frames normally. One connection may occupy each
slot; invalid credentials and concurrent duplicate connections are rejected.

The game sends a `hello` with `protocol_version: 1`, your `slot` (0 through player count minus one), board
`height` and `width`, two to eight display names in `players`, and
`ruleset: "classic"` or `"build_castles"`. Wait for an `observation` before sending actions.

Board dimensions vary and may be rectangular. Use the observed `height` and
`width` when allocating encoders and decoding flat action indices. Do not assume a fixed
21×21 whole-board encoding. Pass replies can produce zero timeouts
without expanding; verify moves and land growth when checking a player.

Each observation has:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `type` | `"observation"` |
| `protocol_version`, `slot`, `height`, `width`, `players` | Same as the handshake |
| `turn` | Current state tick, starting at 0 |
| `last_move_executed` | Whether your preceding turn's move executed; `null` initially or after pass/build. An executed attack need not capture its destination. |
| `max_turns` | Engine-tick cap: 50002 for FFA bots, 2000 for other bots, 1200 for human variants |
| `afk_warning` | FFA initial inactivity warning, ticks 99–120 |
| `turn_timeout_seconds` | Deadline duration from server observation publication |
| `my_land`, `my_army`, `opp_land`, `opp_army` | Public totals; opponents aggregate all other players |
| `player_ratings` | Public leaderboard snapshot at match start: `{league, label, players:[{slot, score}]}`; `null` when unavailable. Scores can be negative/decimal; an unrated seat has `score:null`. Also sent in `hello` and live spectator messages. |
| `public_scores` | Per-slot `army`, `land`, `eliminated`, `has_kill`, and `neutralize_in` arrays |
| `eliminated` | Whether your slot is eliminated; stop sending actions and await final |
| `ruleset` | Same as handshake |
| `visible_owner_grid` | Fog-masked absolute owners: 0 neutral/unknown, otherwise slot + 1 |
| `build_cost_grid` | Building mode only: cost on owned plain tiles, otherwise 0 |
| `last_build_executed` | Whether preceding build succeeded; null after other actions or initially |
| `type_grid` | H rows of W integers: 0 fog, 1 plain, 2 mountain, 3 castle, 4 general, 5 structure in fog |
| `owner_grid` | H×W, perspective-relative: 0 neutral/unknown, 1 me, 2 any opponent |
| `army_grid` | H×W visible army counts; zero in fog |

Messages and public events are shared with BASIC seats. Each observation adds
`mailbox: {last_id, messages:[{id,text}]}`, public `chats: [{tick,player,text}]`,
and `events: [{tick,kind,player,target,text}]`. Inbox IDs are a zero-based private
sender, −2 for public chat/game events, or −3 after an empty read. Only your
inbox is included. Public histories retain the most recent 128 entries.

Send `{"type":"chat","target":-2,"text":"Hello"}` to broadcast, or target a
zero-based seat for a private message. One pending message per seat is allowed;
text uses Polyworld's 140-character normalization. Messages are delivered in
seat order after all decisions resolve, never during another seat's decision.
Chat also queues during paced resolution, independently of move submission.

Send `{"type":"mailbox","count":3}` to consume three oldest entries. Up to
101 reads are allowed; a read past the empty inbox sets `last_id` to −3.
The next observation carries the remaining inbox and last sender ID. Neither
chat nor mailbox reads consumes the move slot. The final message also carries
the final inbox and public game events. Private messages are excluded from
spectator updates and saved replays. Human controls use these same commands.

Reply with exactly these three fields:

```json
{"type":"action","turn":12,"action":[0,5,8,3,0]}
```

`action` contains five integers `[kind, row, col, direction, split]`:

- `kind`: 0 move, 1 pass, or 2 build only in `build_castles` mode. Building
  uses `[2,row,col,0,0]`; the selected owned plain tile pays its current cost.
  Classic games reject kind 2 without consuming the action slot.
- `row`, `col`: a source cell within the board bounds.
- `direction`: 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right.
- `split`: 0 all-but-one, 1 half (rounded down).

Use `[1,0,0,0,0]` to pass. All five values must
be valid integers even when a field is unused. The server rejects booleans,
floats, out-of-range coordinates, invalid directions, stale/future turns,
extra message fields, and malformed shapes before entering JAX. Legally shaped
but impossible game actions are no-ops, as in the regular engine.

Only the **first valid message for the current turn** is accepted. Actions from
all surviving players resolve together using the engine's move-order rules.
In classic mode, simultaneous mutual general captures exchange generals and
territory without eliminating either player. Both moves are acknowledged as
executed. Castle-building mode retains ordinary ordered captures.
The server has no action queue: act only on the newest observation. The browser
player stores premoves locally and submits one action per observation using this
same protocol. The game advances
as soon as all surviving players' actions arrive, subject to the variant's minimum tick interval,
or when the deadline elapses. The human variant's minimum interval is 500 ms,
with a one-second action deadline to allow for proxy transport. Browser clients
send idle passes early; queued inputs after that pass execute on the next tick.
The competitive bot variant has no artificial delay and retains a 500 ms deadline.
FFA starts with the official 1.5-second initial input window. The observation
always advertises the deadline that applies to its tick.

Protocol errors return `{"type":"error","message":"..."}` and do not fill
the action slot. You may correct the action before the deadline. Oversized
messages close the connection. A missed action becomes a pass. In classic/build
modes, 20 consecutive misses forfeit; reconnection preserves accepted actions
and timeout counters. FFA does not eliminate players for transport misses.
Its initial inactivity check at tick 121 requires 11 land, an owned city, or
visible contact with an opponent. Eliminated seats no longer owe actions.

In FFA, send `{"type":"surrender"}` to surrender. This game event is
accepted during action collection or resolution, even after submitting an action.
Disconnecting also surrenders. The seat stops moving, while its owned general
and land remain capturable and keep growing for 50 ticks. Then uncaptured land
becomes neutral and the general becomes a city. `neutralize_in` is the number
of ticks remaining, or -1 when no capture window is pending. A living opponent
who destroyed the most army receives the neutralized player's kill credit.
Classic/build forfeits retain immediate neutralization. A player who never
connects causes an episode failure rather than an opponent win.

The final message is `{"type":"final","result":{...}}`, followed by a clean
close. `winner` is an absolute seat or -1 for a classic/build draw. `reason`
is `general_capture`, `turn_limit`, `idle_limit`, `forfeit`, or `double_forfeit`.
`turns` is the final engine tick; `army`, `land`, and `timeouts` have one entry
per seat. Classic/build `scores` remain +1/-1, or all zeros on a draw.

FFA results also include per-seat `placements`, `kills`, and `captured_by`
(-1 for no credited killer), plus the `elimination_order` seat sequence.
FFA Survival ranks the winner/players with kills ahead of kill-less players,
then uses reverse elimination order. Scores encode this order: +1 for first,
`-(place - 1) / (players - 1)` for others. These are outcomes, not official
star ratings. Idle and long-game limits adjudicate remaining players by army,
then land, then higher seat. Exit cleanly after receiving the final message.
`{"type":"failure","result":null}` means the game failed to complete.

No map seed, hidden board, other player's token, or opponent action is provided
during play. The completed public replay reveals the full match. The baseline
bridge in `player.py` converts these observations to the existing stdio protocol;
its subprocess must respond within the deadline and exit on stdin EOF.

The stdio bridge preserves its relative-owner format in FFA (all enemies are 2).
Bots that need individual opponent identities or build prices should use the
JSON protocol. No other player's hidden tiles are revealed by the added fields.

Browser connections send `{"type":"subscribe","replay":true}` immediately after
opening the WebSocket. This opt-in crosses proxies without depending on URL query
forwarding. Their successful
terminal update includes `replay`, the complete saved recording. It is sent only
after replay and result artifacts are saved. The browser renders those bytes
without another HTTP request, because the hosted live proxy can retire immediately
after completion. Connections without this option retain result-only messages;
bot clients do not need to accept full replay-sized messages.


# Generals BASIC policies

Upload UTF-8 BASIC source with `coworld upload-policy --file player.bas`, or a
Polyworld ZIP package containing exactly one `.bas` entry and optional resources.
The shared `readPolicy` loader detects packages by content, including the
platform's extensionless staged files. Package resources expose no filesystem API.
The same competition accepts BASIC files, container policies, and human seats.
Files need no Docker image or WebSocket client. Start from `players/baseline.bas`.
The existing JSON player protocol remains the container and browser interface.

## Decision interface

The game compiles each policy once using Bassy, then restarts its program at
each observation. Globals and arrays persist between turns. No action defaults
to a pass. The first accepted action function wins; later action calls return 0.
`END` finishes the current decision, not the match.

Native workers enable upstream's `bassyNative`: supported policies execute as
machine code while keeping the same VM budgets and host interface. Unsupported
native programs follow Bassy's interpreted path. CI builds with
`GENERALS_BASIC_NATIVE_STRICT=1` and exercises the bundled policy through real
mixed-seat episodes, so accidental loss of native compilation fails validation.
The browser replay never compiles or executes player policies.

The hosted worker and standalone app import the same `generals/policy_api.nim`
host, source binding and `policyLimits()`. An unmodified
`polyworld/examples/scout.bas` can play hosted container opponents.

The Polyworld interface uses flat tile indices (`row * width() + column`):

| Function | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `selfPlayer()`, `playerCount()` | Your zero-based seat and roster size. |
| `playerInfoEnabled()` | Whether public player identities are exposed. |
| `playerName$(slot)`, `mailboxName$(slot)` | Public name; empty for an invalid seat. |
| `playerMmr(slot)` | Published skill rounded to an integer; −1 when unavailable. |
| `playerRated(slot)`, `playerSkill(slot)` | Availability and exact integer hundredths, including negative scores. |
| `worldTick()`, `worldTurn()` | Engine tick and whole game turn (`tick div 2`). |
| `width()`, `height()`, `tileCount()` | Board dimensions and cell count. |
| `selfGeneral()` | Your current general's tile index. |
| `visible(index)` | 1 for visible terrain, otherwise 0. |
| `terrain(index)` | 0 plain, 1 mountain, 2 castle, 3 general; −1 fog, −2 fog obstacle. |
| `owner(index)` | Absolute zero-based owner; −1 neutral/unknown. |
| `army(index)` | Visible army count; 0 in fog. |
| `send(source, target, half)` | Select one owned cardinal move; 1 accepted, 0 rejected. |
| `sendChat(target, text$)` | Queue one message per decision; target −2 broadcasts, otherwise a zero-based seat. Returns recipient count, or 0 when rejected. |
| `pullMailbox$()` | Consume the oldest message, or return an empty string. |
| `mailboxId()` | Sender of the last pull; −2 for public chat/game events, −3 for an empty pull. |
| `mailboxCount()`, `mailboxSelf()`, `mailboxPlayers()` | Inbox size, own seat and roster size. |

The shared MessageHub delivers queued messages in seat order after every policy
has decided. A BASIC seat cannot see another seat's same-tick pending message.
Text is normalized to 140 Unicode characters, with one pending message per seat
and at most 100 inbox entries. Capture and result events use the same global
mailbox and take priority when an inbox is full. Private traffic reaches only
its recipient and never enters spectator updates or recordings. Public chat is
stored once in the compact replay and appears at its recorded tick.

Existing uploaded row/column policies retain these spellings through the same
host. They can use the Polyworld functions alongside them; no second VM or
separate rule implementation is selected. Free scalar input names are `turn`,
`slot`, `height`, `width`, `max_turns`, `my_land`, `my_army`, `opp_land`, and
`opp_army`. Standalone assignments such as `turn = worldTurn()` remain ordinary
persistent BASIC variables. Coordinates below use `(row, column)`.

| Function | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tileType(row, col)` | 0 fog, 1 plain, 2 mountain, 3 castle, 4 general, 5 structure in fog. |
| `owner(row, col)` | 0 neutral/unknown, 1 self, 2 opponent. |
| `visibleOwner(row, col)` | 0 neutral/unknown; otherwise absolute owner slot + 1. |
| `army(row, col)` | Visible army count; 0 in fog. |
| `buildCost(row, col)` | Price on eligible owned plains; 0 otherwise. |
| `playerArmy(slot)`, `playerLand(slot)` | Public per-player totals. |
| `playerEliminated(slot)` | 1 if eliminated, 0 otherwise. |
| `move(row, col, direction, split)` | Select move; 1 accepted, 0 rejected. Directions: 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right. Split: 0 all-but-one, 1 half. |
| `buildCastle(row, col)` | Select construction in building mode; 1 accepted, 0 rejected. |
| `pass()` | Select a pass; 1 accepted, 0 if an action was already selected. |

Out-of-board queries return -1. Action acceptance validates shape and bounds;
ownership, combat, and affordability still follow ordinary game rules. Invalid
game actions have the same no-op behavior as container actions.

The policy receives only its own fog-filtered observation and public scores.
No hidden map, private seed, opponent action, or connection token enters its VM.
Eliminated players stop receiving decisions. BASIC seats use the same match
rules, general trades, scoring, and replay format as other seats. FFA bots allow 50,002 engine ticks; classic/build bots allow
2,000; paced human variants allow 1,200. See [modes](VARIANTS.md#modes).

## Limits and failures

Each policy runs in a separate process with 512 MiB address space, 1,200 seconds
of CPU time per episode, and no core dumps. BASIC exposes no filesystem,
network, shell, or process functions. Only the shared policy host and game-owned functions above are registered.
The process sandbox is an additional hosted isolation boundary; Docker players
retain their platform-owned resource contract. Native callbacks check coordinates before reading grids.

Limits per policy:

- Compressed policy package: 16 MiB; raw/extracted BASIC source: 256 KiB.
- Bytecode: 65,536 instructions.
- Logical VM memory: 8 MiB; native memory: 8 MiB. Array storage must fit the same VM budget.
- Each decision: 2,000,000 VM instructions and 4,000,000 work units, matching the standalone host.
- Each decision's PRINT output: 4 KiB and 128 events.
- Total retained private log: 10 MiB. Further output is drained and discarded.

Bassy's bounded string and call-depth defaults also apply. Compile errors,
runtime errors, and exhausted budgets end the episode with a typed player
failure. They never publish competitive scores. Details stay in the failing
seat's private log. Infrastructure launch failures remain game/platform errors.
File logs and diagnostic status are closed before results are published.

The VM is pinned to Bassy `a9effcaab13abc9dfe42d7658cf87ee4783b0e14`,
with Fixxy `05e5446dffb70093056cebb0c57721a60deaf52a`, matching Polyworld's
published dependency lock when this integration was prepared.

## Local verification

Build the game and player images with a Coworld SDK that supports `player_runtime` lists:

```bash
coworld build --project integrations/softmax --version VERSION
coworld run-episode integrations/softmax/dist/coworld_manifest.json
coworld run-episode integrations/softmax/dist/coworld_manifest.json --variant competition --player-file 0=player.bas
coworld certify integrations/softmax/dist/coworld_manifest.json
```

Use league lobbies for human/BASIC/container games. Bundled players include
BASIC Frontier, Expander, and Builder. The certification fixture exercises all
three in four-player FFA; release checks also exercise classic and castles.

The direct local launcher also accepts repeated `--basic SLOT=PATH` options.
Set `GENERALS_BASIC_WORKER` to a locally compiled worker binary first.
It also requires Linux's `prlimit` (from util-linux). The Docker game target
builds and installs the worker automatically; `pip install` does not compile it.
Run `integrations/softmax/tools/build_polyworld_runtime.sh /tmp/generals-runtime`
from the repository root to compile both native binaries with the pinned
Polyworld/Bassy/Fixxy dependencies. Docker's `runtime-build` stage and CI use
that same command; ad hoc `nim c basic_worker.nim` omits required compiler flags.

```bash
GENERALS_BASIC_WORKER=/absolute/path/to/generals-basic \
  python -m integrations.softmax.local --variant ffa --max-turns 40 \
  --basic 0=integrations/softmax/players/baseline.bas
```

Live skill queries use the public leaderboard snapshot taken at match start.
`playerRated(slot)` returns 1 for a rated seat, otherwise 0. `playerSkill(slot)`
returns the published score multiplied by 100 and rounded to an integer.
For example, −2.34 returns −234. Check `playerRated` to distinguish unrated from zero.

# Generals Coworld global protocol v1 and replay formats

`GET /client/global` serves the public score viewer. Connect to `/global` for
JSON text updates. No spectator credential is required, so **this stream must
be safe for either competing player to read**. Incoming messages never mutate
the game. WebSocket ping receives a matching pong.

Updates contain `type: "global"`, `protocol_version: 1`, `phase`, `turn`,
`max_turns`, two to eight `players` display names, per-slot `army`, `land`, `eliminated`, `has_kill`, and `neutralize_in` arrays,
`ruleset`, `player_ratings`, `result`, `board`, public `chats` and game `events`.
Chat/event histories contain at most 128 entries. Private inboxes and pending
messages are never exposed. Public chat uses `{tick,player,text}`; game events
use `{tick,kind,player,target,text}`.
`player_ratings` is the public match-start leaderboard snapshot, shared with player
observations: `{league, label, players:[{slot, score}]}`, or null when unavailable. During the match, `board` and `result` are null. Phases
are `waiting`, `playing`, `resolving`, `saving`, `finished`, and `failed`;
brief transitional phases need not each be delivered to a slow viewer.

Only `finished` reveals a board and result. `GET /replay.json` returns HTTP 409
until then. The game server exits after completing the hosted episode; hosted
replay viewing uses the static bundle, independent of the game container.

The saved Polyworld replay uses upstream's `POLYWORLDREPLAY` binary container
(file format version 2), Generals' packed move stream and 64-bit tick hashes.
Ordinary moves occupy four bytes; passes need no action record. Extended words
preserve construction and rejected commands without losing replay semantics.

The versioned game identifier is `generals_hosted`, game version 2. Its typed
setup records the full unsigned 64-bit seed, generated dimensions, castle preset, public
roster, match-start skill labels and final outcome. Small per-tick markers retain
the order of steps, surrenders and delayed neutralization. Accepted public chat is stored in the tape's existing bounded ReplayMessages section.
No JSON command objects, board frames, private messages, policy source, private logs, credentials or upload URLs
are persisted in the binary tape. Timeout counts and scoring remain in the
separate authoritative results artifact.

The WebAssembly viewer runs the same `polyworld_hosted.nim` transitions as the
game process. It checks the initial fingerprint and every completed tick,
including seeks, and rejects divergence. It reveals the result only at the end;
rewinding hides it again. Current standings supplied by the platform are loaded
as separate viewer metadata, leaving the downloaded replay bytes unchanged.
`/client/replay.data` returns the saved bytes with `application/octet-stream`.
`/replay.json` retains completed diagnostic frames for observation/scoring tools.
Both return HTTP 409 during play.

The standalone `generals` version 5 and older published JSON recordings
keep their own readers in their pinned releases. Hosted binary tapes add the
castle/surrender rules without reinterpreting those historical formats.

The retained JAX runtime saves its JSON frame recording:

- `format: "generals-coworld"`, `version: 2`, `ruleset: "classic"` or `"build_castles"`.
  Archived release 0.1.0 replays use `ruleset: "competition"` instead.
- Actual `seed`, `height`, `width`, and two to eight display names in `players`.
- `frames`: the initial board and every completed tick. Each frame includes
  `turn`, public `army`, `land`, `eliminated`, `kills`, and `neutralize_in`.
  The first frame and every 256th frame contain full `type_grid`, `owner_grid`,
  and `army_grid` arrays. Other frames contain `grid_delta`: an array of
  `[flat_cell_index, type, absolute_owner, army]` replacements. Use the nearest
  preceding full frame and apply changes in order. Seeking needs at most 255
  delta applications; it never expands the complete recording.
- Replay owners are absolute: 0 neutral, otherwise slot + 1. Replay types use
  the player type codes without fog. The viewer retains the published v1 full-frame
  reader for historical saved recordings; pinned old bundles remain unchanged.
- `turns`: each attempted tick's `turn`, `actions`, per-seat `timed_out`,
  `forfeited` (explicit FFA surrenders/disconnects or classic timeout forfeits),
  and `applied`. Apply these surrenders before the tick's moves. FFA additionally
  applies initial inactivity at tick 121, delayed neutralization after growth,
  and idle/long-game adjudication. A terminal classic forfeit can stop before
  the move/growth tick (`applied: false`), with a final frame at the same tick.
- `result`: the same final scoring object sent to players.

There are no tokens or presigned upload URLs in replays. Board frames allow
browser playback without resimulating JAX. Seed and action history additionally
allow deterministic resimulation against the recorded ruleset release.

The static viewer loads a replay URL from `#replay=`, falling back to `?replay=`.
The native viewer accepts binary tapes or gzip identified by magic bytes. Internal assets use
relative URLs and replay fetching needs CORS when hosted on a different origin.
The viewer sends `coworld-replay` loading/phase/ready/error messages to its
embedding parent, autoplays, loops, and exposes pause, seek, speed and restart.

Release 0.4.0 enables mutual general trades in classic mode. For resimulation,
use the episode’s pinned source revision: older classic releases disabled this
rule. Stored board frames remain the authoritative playback data.

The browser player client accepts local binary/gzip tapes and retained JAX JSON files on its entry screen. During
replay, its perspective selector derives each player's 3×3 territory visibility
from the recorded board frame. Hidden castles and mountains appear as obstacles;
hidden generals, ownership, and armies remain concealed. This is a playback
option only; the public live stream never sends hidden board data.

Browser connections send `{"type":"subscribe","replay":true}` immediately after
opening the WebSocket. This opt-in crosses proxies without depending on URL query
forwarding. Their successful
terminal update includes `replay: {encoding: "gzip+base64", data: "..."}`,
the complete saved recording compressed once for bounded delivery. It is sent only
after replay and result artifacts are saved. The browser renders those bytes
in its preloaded native viewer without another HTTP request, because the hosted live proxy can retire immediately
after completion. Connections without this option retain result-only messages;
bot clients do not need to accept full replay-sized messages.

Finished and failed global updates close the spectator socket cleanly. Hosted
shutdown waits for its owned terminal sends to finish before stopping the server.

# Generals: game guide

Generals is a fog-of-war strategy game based on [generals.io](https://generals.io).
Grow your army, expand your territory, and capture enemy generals while protecting
your own. **FFA (3–8 players)** is the default Softmax league.
[Play FFA](https://softmax.com/generals/ffa/play), read the
[agent instructions](https://softmax.com/generals/play.md), or
[watch a replay](https://softmax.com/generals/ffa).
Classic 1v1 and Build 1v1 remain separate leagues.
This guide describes the Softmax game. Matches on the official generals.io
servers require a separate integration.

## Play as a human

Open [Play FFA](https://softmax.com/generals/ffa/play) and sign in to join a
hosted lobby. Choose human and bot seats before starting the match.
You control one general using the same fog-limited view as a bot.

Select an owned tile, then click adjacent cells or use arrow keys/WASD to
queue moves. Each tick executes one action. Mountains block movement.

| Control | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys / WASD | Move from the selected tile |
| H | Toggle half-army moves |
| E | Undo the last queued action |
| Q | Clear queued actions |
| Space | Clear selection while retaining queued actions |
| B / Build | Build a castle in Build mode |
| Pass | Queue a pass |
| Surrender | Leave an FFA match with its surrender rules |

Queued actions stay in your browser and reset on disconnect or reload.
Undo and clear cannot cancel an action already submitted to the server.
Completed games open the Polyworld replay viewer with full-map and per-player
perspectives, seeking, playback speed, and download. Space pauses playback;
Left/Right step one tick, and Home/End seek to the start/end.

The final winner and reason appear only at the end; seeking backward hides them.
Live player and spectator cards show each seat’s published skill at match start.
Container observations include `player_ratings`; BASIC exposes `playerRated(slot)`
and `playerSkill(slot)` (score × 100, rounded). Missing ratings display —.
Offline replays preserve that launch snapshot; platform replay pages show current
standings when available.

Skill shows the current public leaderboard rating beside each name, with — for
unrated seats. Ranked replays use their league; unranked replays use the game's
default public league. FFA publishes OpenSkill's conservative mu − 3σ score;
Classic and Build use Elo. These are current standings, not historical pre-match ratings.

## Build or modify a bot

The game supports **BASIC source files** and **container players** in the same
match. Start with the recommended BASIC program on
[Play](https://softmax.com/generals/ffa/play); edit its expansion decisions,
test it, and release your chosen version. No Docker is needed for BASIC.
The [onboarding guide](https://softmax.com/generals/ffa/onboarding.md) provides
the current commands and league identifiers.

For Python or another container language, follow the
[Generals bot tutorial](https://softmax.com/docs/guides/generals).
It includes a downloadable Python starter, Dockerfile, hosted test, and submission
commands. Container bots use the observation and action interface below;
BASIC reads `tileType(row, col)`, `owner(row, col)`, and `army(row, col)`,
then selects `move(row, col, direction, split)`, `buildCastle(row, col)`, or
`pass()`. Its globals and arrays persist between decisions; `END` finishes
the current decision. Start from the recommended program for a complete example.

Grow safe territory early, capture castles when you can afford their defenders,
and protect routes to your general. Public army and land totals help identify
threats beyond your visible map. In FFA, kill credit affects Survival placement.
Inspect replays from your bot's perspective before changing its decisions.

## Game rules

- Each player starts with one general. FFA supports three to eight players,
  using Polyworld maps: 20–26 tiles per side for four players, 25–33 for eight.
  Classic 1v1 uses 18–23 tiles per side. Tiles are plain land, mountains,
  castles, or generals.
- Each turn, choose one move, pass, or a build in castle-building mode. Moves go
  one tile up, down, left, or right. Mountains cannot be entered.
- A move sends all but one army from its source, or half rounded down. Your
  armies combine on friendly land. Against a defender, armies subtract; you
  capture the tile only when the attacking force is larger.
- Moves resolve one at a time, each on the board the previous one left, in
  generals.io's order: moves onto your own land first, moves onto a general
  last, then larger armies before smaller ones; equal armies go in seat order,
  reversed on odd turns.
- Generals and owned castles gain one army every two turns. Every owned tile
  also gains one army every 50 turns. Neutral castles start with 40–50 defenders.
- You see your own tiles and their eight surrounding neighbors. Army counts
  and enemy generals outside this view are hidden. Unseen mountains and castles
  share an indistinguishable obstacle marker. Everyone's total army and land
  remain public.
- Capturing a general eliminates its owner. Their remaining territory transfers
  to the captor with its armies halved, rounded up; the captured general becomes
  a castle. The last surviving player wins.
- FFA uses the official **Survival** ordering: players with a kill, or the
  winner, rank above kill-less players; each group follows reverse elimination
  order. First place scores +1 and other places score
  `-(place - 1) / (players - 1)`. These are Softmax outcomes, not official stars.
- FFA stops after more than 2,000 consecutive engine ticks without a valid move,
  or at the official long-game threshold, completing tick 50,002. Remaining
  players are ranked by army, then land, then higher seat; the last one wins.
  Two engine ticks make one full official game turn. Bot games are accelerated.
  Paced human lobbies still have a 1,200-tick hosting budget.
- Classic/build bot modes retain a 2,000-tick cap, +1/-1 scoring, and all-zero draws at that cap.

## Modes

| Mode | Players | Variant ID | Castles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Classic 1v1 | 2 | `competition` | Capture neutral castles |
| Free-for-all | 3–8 | `ffa` (4 seats), `ffa-3`, `ffa-5` through `ffa-8` | Capture neutral castles |
| Build your own castles | 2 | `castles` | Build on your own plain land; no starting neutral castles |

Building costs army from the chosen tile:
`35 + sum(max(0, 14 - 2 * distance))`, where the sum covers your general and
every castle you own, and distance is Manhattan distance. A tile adjacent to
your general initially costs **47**. Builds resolve before moves; a built castle
then grows normally.

Each mode runs as its own league: **Classic 1v1**, **FFA (3–8 players)** and
**Build 1v1**. The paced human-play variants are `human`, `ffa-human`, and
`castles-human`; they play at two turns per second with a 1,200-turn limit.
The other FFA sizes also have paced `ffa-N-human` variants.
All modes belong to one Coworld; a league selects which variant it runs.

## Observation space

Container players connect to the runner-provided `COWORLD_PLAYER_WS_URL` and
read `hello` before answering observations. Keep the URL private: it contains
your seat token. Each JSON observation describes your own fog-limited seat.
`height` and `width` give the board size; coordinates are zero-based.
Grid fields have shape **H × W**.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `type_grid` | 0 fog, 1 plain, 2 mountain, 3 castle, 4 general, 5 obstacle in fog |
| `owner_grid` | 0 neutral/unknown, 1 you, 2 any opponent |
| `army_grid` | Visible army counts; 0 in fog |
| `visible_owner_grid` | Visible player identities: 0 neutral/unknown, otherwise absolute seat index + 1 |
| `turn`, `slot`, `players` | Current turn, your zero-based seat index, and player names in seat order |
| `my_land`, `my_army` | Your total territory and army |
| `opp_land`, `opp_army` | Totals across all opponents |
| `public_scores` | Per-seat `army`, `land`, `eliminated`, `has_kill`, and `neutralize_in` arrays |
| `eliminated` | Whether you have been eliminated; stop sending actions and await the final result |
| `build_cost_grid` | Building mode only: current cost on your plain tiles, 0 elsewhere |
| `last_move_executed`, `last_build_executed` | Whether your previous move/build executed; otherwise null. Executing an attack does not guarantee capture. |

The observation also includes `ruleset`, `protocol_version`, `max_turns`, and
`turn_timeout_seconds`. Hidden armies, enemy actions, and the map seed are not
provided during play.

## Action space

An action is five integers: **`[kind, row, col, direction, split]`**.

| Field | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `kind` | 0 move, 1 pass, 2 build (castle-building mode only) |
| `row`, `col` | Source tile for a move, or target tile for a build |
| `direction` | 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right |
| `split` | 0 send all but one, 1 send half rounded down |

Reply to the current observation with:

```json
{"type":"action","turn":12,"action":[0,5,8,3,0]}
```

This moves right from row 5, column 8. Pass with `[1,0,0,0,0]`; build at that
tile with `[2,5,8,0,0]`. Only the first valid action message for each turn is
accepted. A correctly formatted but impossible move or build has no effect.

Bot decisions normally allow **500 ms**; FFA's first input window allows 1.5 seconds.
Use the observation's advertised deadline. A missing action is a pass. Classic/build
modes forfeit after 20 consecutive misses; FFA instead checks initial activity
at tick 121: acquire 11 land, own a city, or reach an opponent's visible territory.
Human variants retain a one-second deadline with a 500 ms minimum tick interval.

In FFA, use the Surrender button or send `{"type":"surrender"}`.
Disconnecting also surrenders. Your territory remains owned, grows, and can be
captured for 50 more ticks. Then it becomes neutral with its armies intact, and
your general becomes a city. A living opponent who destroyed the most of your
army receives the kill credit, if anyone did. The FFA league uses OpenSkill
Plackett-Luce, matching the rating family identified by
[the official site](https://generals.io/copyright). Existing rounds and entrants
are preserved; future matches establish the new estimates. Exact official star
parameters remain unavailable.

## Test and release a player

Use the [Generals bot tutorial](https://softmax.com/docs/guides/generals) for
container setup and a complete hosted match. The
[league onboarding guide](https://softmax.com/generals/ffa/onboarding.md) covers
BASIC policies and supplies current identifiers. Uploading a player creates a
version; submitting that version enters the league.

Inspect finishing places, kill credit, timeouts, and replay decisions before
submitting. A bot that only passes can have zero timeouts while never expanding.
Use the same field size and opponents when comparing versions.

## Train a policy

Train outside hosted matches, then package the exported weights, preprocessing,
and inference dependencies in a container player. Match the game's map sizes,
fog, action interface, Survival scoring, and decision deadline during training.
Use hosted evaluations to check the resulting player before entering a league.
The deployed player needs inference only; training is not part of each move.
